title.zh: 卷二百〇三 列傳第九十: 方技 工藝
title.en: Volume 203 Biographies 90: Medicine and Divination, Arts and Crafts
title.raw: 卷二百〇三 列傳第九十: 方技 工藝 Volume 203 Biographies 90: Medicine and Divination, Arts and Crafts

sentences.zh: 自昔帝王勃興，雖星曆醫卜方術異能之士，莫不過絕於人，類非後來所及，蓋天運也。

translations.literal: From antiquity when emperors rose vigorously, even specialists in astronomy, medicine, divination, arts, and extraordinary abilities all surpassed ordinary men; such men were generally not matched by those who came later — this was heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever emperors have risen to power in ages past, experts in astronomy, medicine, divination, and the occult arts have invariably stood head and shoulders above their contemporaries — gifts few later generations could match, shaped by heaven's own design.

sentences.zh: 元有中土，巨公異人，身兼數器者，皆應期而出，相與立法創制，開物成務，以輔成大業，亦云盛哉。

translations.literal: When the Yuan held the Central Plains, great lords and extraordinary men who combined many skills all appeared in response to the times, together establishing laws and creating institutions, opening things and completing affairs, to assist in accomplishing the great enterprise — how splendid indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan in China, remarkable men who mastered many disciplines appeared as if on cue, joining together to frame laws, devise institutions, and advance civilization in support of the dynasty's founding triumph — a flourishing age indeed.

sentences.zh: 若道流釋子，所挾多方，事適逢時，既皆別為之傳。

translations.literal: As for Taoist clergy and Buddhist monks, who possessed many methods and whose affairs happened to suit the times, separate biographies have already been written for them.
translations.idiomatic: Taoist priests and Buddhist monks, each with their own wide-ranging arts and timely rise to prominence, already have separate biographies elsewhere in these annals.

sentences.zh: 其他以術數言事輒驗，及以醫著效，被光寵者甚眾。

translations.literal: Others who spoke of affairs through numerology and arts and were immediately verified, and those who achieved renown through medicine, were very numerous in receiving imperial favor.
translations.idiomatic: Countless others won imperial favor by foretelling events through divination with uncanny accuracy, or by achieving conspicuous success in medicine.

sentences.zh: 舊史多闕弗錄，今取其事蹟可見者，為《方技篇》。

translations.literal: The old histories mostly omitted and did not record them; now we take those whose deeds are visible and compile the "Treatise on Arts and Techniques."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories largely passed them over; here we gather those whose careers can still be traced into this chapter on medicine, divination, and the technical arts.

sentences.zh: 而以工藝貴顯，亦附見焉。

translations.literal: Those who attained eminence through craftsmanship are also appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Those who rose to distinction through the practical arts are included here as well.

sentences.zh: 田忠良，字正卿，其先平陽趙城人，金亡，徙中山。

translations.literal: Tian Zhongliang, courtesy name Zhengqing, was originally from Zhaocheng in Pingyang; after the fall of the Jin, his family moved to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhongliang, styled Zhengqing, came from a family originally of Zhaocheng in Pingyang; when the Jin dynasty fell, they relocated to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 忠良好學，通儒家、雜家言。

translations.literal: Zhongliang loved learning and was versed in Confucian and miscellaneous school teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang was a devoted scholar, well versed in both Confucian classics and the eclectic learning of the miscellaneous schools.

sentences.zh: 嘗識太保劉秉忠於微時。

translations.literal: He had once known Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong in his days of obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: He had known Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong long before Liu rose to power.

sentences.zh: 秉忠薦於世祖，遣使召至，帝視其狀貌步趨，顧謂侍臣曰：「是雖以陰陽家進，必將為國用。」

translations.literal: Bingzhong recommended him to Shizu; the emperor sent an envoy to summon him. The emperor observed his appearance and gait, turned to his attendants and said: "Though this man advances through the Yin-Yang school, he will surely serve the state."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong recommended him to Kublai Khan, who sent for him. When Zhongliang arrived, the emperor studied his bearing and stride and told his attendants, "He may have come up through the arts of yin and yang, but he will prove indispensable to the realm."

sentences.zh: 俄指西序第二人謂忠良曰： 「彼手中握何物？」

translations.literal: Shortly he pointed to the second man on the western side and said to Zhongliang: "What is that man holding in his hand?"
translations.idiomatic: Then he pointed to the second man seated on the west side and asked Zhongliang, "What is he holding in his hand?"

sentences.zh: 忠良對曰：「雞卵也。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "A chicken egg."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang answered, "A hen's egg."

sentences.zh: 果然。

translations.literal: It was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，又曰：「朕有事縈心，汝試占之。」

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and said again: "I have something weighing on my mind — try divining it."
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor said, "Something has been troubling me — try your divination on it."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「以臣術推之，當是一名僧病耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "By my art I infer it must be the illness of a certain monk.
translations.idiomatic: By my reckoning," he replied, "it concerns the illness of a monk.

sentences.zh: 「帝曰：「然，國師也。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "So it is — the Imperial Preceptor."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Exactly — the Imperial Preceptor."

sentences.zh: 遂遣左侍儀奉御也先乃送忠良司天台，給筆札，令秉忠試星曆、遁甲諸書。

translations.literal: He then sent the Left Attendant of Ceremonial Yexianai to escort Zhongliang to the Directorate of Astronomy, provided writing materials, and had Bingzhong test him on books of astronomy, calendrics, and dunjia.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Yexianai, attendant of the Left Ceremonial Office, escort Zhongliang to the Directorate of Astronomy, supplied him with writing materials, and ordered Liu Bingzhong to examine him in astronomy, calendrics, and the dunjia arts.

sentences.zh: 秉忠奏曰：「所試皆通，司天諸生鮮有及者。」

translations.literal: Bingzhong memorialized: "In all that was tested he is thoroughly versed; few among the students of the Directorate of Astronomy can match him."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bingzhong reported, "He has mastered every subject tested — few students at the Directorate of Astronomy can equal him."

sentences.zh: 詔官之司天。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him to office in the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed him to a post at the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕用兵江南，困於襄樊，累年不決，奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I am campaigning in the south against Jiangnan, bogged down at Xiang and Fan for years without resolution — what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Our armies in the south have been stalled at Xiangyang and Fancheng for years with no end in sight — what can be done?"

sentences.zh: 忠良對曰：「在酉年矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "It will be in the year of the rooster."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang answered, "Victory will come in the year of the rooster."

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，阿里海牙奏請率十萬眾渡江，朝議難之，帝密問曰：「汝試筮之，濟否？」

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan, Alihaiya memorialized requesting to lead a hundred thousand men across the Yangtze; the court deliberated and found it difficult. The emperor secretly asked: "Try divining for me — will they succeed in crossing?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan (1274), Alihaiya petitioned to lead a hundred thousand troops across the Yangtze; the court was divided. The emperor asked Zhongliang privately, "Divine for me — will the crossing succeed?"

sentences.zh: 忠良對曰：「濟。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "They will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: "They will," Zhongliang replied."

sentences.zh: 帝獵於柳林，禦幄殿，侍臣甚眾，顧忠良曰：「今拜一大將取江南，朕心已定，果何人耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor was hunting at Willow Grove, in the imperial tent hall with many attendants present. He turned to Zhongliang and said: "I am now appointing a great general to take Jiangnan; my mind is already made up — who is it in truth?"
translations.idiomatic: While hunting at Willow Grove, the emperor sat in his tent surrounded by attendants and asked Zhongliang, "I have decided to appoint a great general to conquer the south — who is it, in your judgment?"

sentences.zh: 忠良環視左右，目一人，對曰：「是偉丈夫，可屬大事。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang looked around to left and right, fixed his gaze on one man, and replied: "This is a great man who can be entrusted with a great affair."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang scanned those around him, fixed on one man, and said, "There stands the man — a commanding figure fit to bear a great charge."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「此伯顏也，為西王旭烈兀使，朕以其才留用之，汝識朕心。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said: "This is Bayan — he came as envoy for the Western Prince Hulagu; I kept him for his talent. You know my mind."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed. "That is Bayan — he came as envoy from Prince Hulagu in the west, and I kept him for his ability. You read my thoughts well."

sentences.zh: 賜鈔五百貫、衣一襲。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred strings of paper money and one suit of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with five hundred strings of paper money and a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 七月十五日夜，白氣貫三台，帝問何祥，忠良對曰：「三公其死乎！」

translations.literal: On the night of the fifteenth day of the seventh month, a white vapor pierced the Three Terraces; the emperor asked what omen this was. Zhongliang replied: "Will the Three Dukes die?"
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the fifteenth of the seventh month, a white comet streaked through the Three Terraces constellation. When the emperor asked what it portended, Zhongliang said, "Surely one of the Three Dukes is about to die!"

sentences.zh: 未幾，太保劉秉忠卒。

translations.literal: Before long, Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Grand Preceptor Liu Bingzhong died.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝出獵，駐輦召忠良曰：「朕有所遺，汝知何物，還可復得否？」

translations.literal: In the eighth month the emperor went out hunting; halting his carriage he summoned Zhongliang and said: "I have lost something — do you know what it is, and whether it can be recovered?"
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, while out hunting, the emperor halted his carriage and called Zhongliang. "I have lost something," he said. "Do you know what it is, and whether I shall get it back?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「其數珠乎？

translations.literal: He replied: "Is it your prayer beads?
translations.idiomatic: "Your prayer beads?" he replied.

sentences.zh: 明日，二十里外人當有得而來獻者。」

translations.literal: Tomorrow someone twenty li away will find them and come to present them."
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow someone twenty li distant will find them and bring them to you."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: And so it indeed came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: And so it happened.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，賜以貂裘。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and bestowed a sable fur coat on him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and gave him a sable fur coat.

sentences.zh: 十月，有旨問忠良：「南征將士能渡江否？

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict questioned Zhongliang: "Can the southern campaign troops cross the Yangtze?
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the emperor asked Zhongliang by edict, "Can our southern expedition cross the Yangtze?

sentences.zh: 勞師費財，朕甚憂之。」

translations.literal: The army is worn and finances exhausted — I am deeply troubled."
translations.idiomatic: The campaign strains our troops and drains our treasury — I am deeply worried."

sentences.zh: 忠良奏曰：「明年正月當奏捷矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang memorialized: "In the first month of next year victory will be reported."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang replied, "Victory will be reported in the first month of next year."

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，師取鄂州，丞相伯顏遣使來獻宋寶，有玉香爐，輟以賜忠良，及金織文十匹。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year the army took Ezhou; Chancellor Bayan sent an envoy to present Song treasures, including a jade incense burner, which he set aside to bestow on Zhongliang, along with ten bolts of gold brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year (1275) the army captured Ezhou. Chancellor Bayan sent tribute from the Song, including a jade incense burner, which he reserved for Zhongliang along with ten bolts of gold brocade.

sentences.zh: 二月，帝不豫，召忠良謂曰：「或言朕今歲不嘉，汝術云何？」

translations.literal: In the second month the emperor was unwell; he summoned Zhongliang and said: "Some say this year is inauspicious for me — what does your art say?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the emperor fell ill and summoned Zhongliang. "Some say this year bodes ill for me," he said. "What does your art tell you?"

sentences.zh: 忠良對曰：「聖體行自安矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "Your sacred person will soon be at ease."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty will soon recover," Zhongliang answered."

sentences.zh: 三月，帝疾愈，賜銀五百兩、衣材三十匹。

translations.literal: In the third month the emperor's illness abated; he granted five hundred taels of silver and thirty bolts of clothing material.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor recovered and rewarded him with five hundred taels of silver and thirty bolts of fabric for robes.

sentences.zh: 五月，車駕清暑上都，遣使來召曰：「叛者浸入山陵，久而不去，汝與和禮霍孫率眾往視之。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month the imperial carriage went to Shangdu for summer respite; an envoy was sent to summon him with the message: "Rebels have penetrated the imperial tombs and linger without departing — you and Holihosun lead troops to inspect."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the court retired to Shangdu for the summer. An envoy summoned Zhongliang: "Rebels have entered the imperial tombs and will not leave — take Holihosun and a force to investigate."

sentences.zh: 既至，山陵如故，俄而叛兵大至，圍之三匝，三日不解。

translations.literal: When they arrived the tombs were as before; soon rebel troops came in great force, encircling them three deep, and for three days the siege was not lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived the tombs were undisturbed, but rebel forces soon appeared in strength, surrounding them three deep for three days without relief.

sentences.zh: 忠良引眾夜歸，敵殊不覺，和禮霍孫以為神，白其事於帝，賜黃金十兩。

translations.literal: Zhongliang led his men back by night; the enemy did not notice at all. Holihosun regarded it as miraculous, reported the affair to the emperor, and he was granted ten taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang led his men out by night without the enemy detecting them. Holihosun took it for a miracle, reported the exploit to the emperor, and Zhongliang received ten taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 八月，以海都為邊患，遣皇子北平王那木罕、丞相安童征之，忠良奏曰：「不吉，將有叛者。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, because Haidu was a border menace, the Prince of Beiping Namuhan and Chancellor Antong were sent to campaign against him. Zhongliang memorialized: "It is inauspicious — there will be rebels."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, with Haidu threatening the frontier, the Prince of Beiping Namuhan and Chancellor Antong were dispatched against him. Zhongliang warned, "The omens are bad — rebellion will follow."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諸王昔里吉劫皇子、丞相以入海都，帝召忠良曰：「朕幾信讒言罪汝，今如汝言，汝祀神致禱，雖黃金朕所不吝。」

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Prince Shiregi seized the prince and chancellor and took them to Haidu. The emperor summoned Zhongliang and said: "I nearly believed slander and punished you; now it is as you said. Offer sacrifices to the spirits and pray — though it be gold, I shall not be sparing."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Prince Shiregi seized the prince and chancellor and delivered them to Haidu. The emperor summoned Zhongliang: "I nearly believed your enemies and punished you; events have proved you right. Pray to the spirits on our behalf — ask for whatever gold you need."

sentences.zh: 忠良對曰：「無事於神，皇子未年當還。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "There is no need to trouble the spirits — the prince will return before the year is out."
translations.idiomatic: "No need to trouble the spirits," Zhongliang said. "The prince will return before year's end."

sentences.zh: 後果然。

translations.literal: And afterward it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 十四年八月，車駕駐隆興北，忠良奏曰：「昔里吉之叛，以安童之食不彼及也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year the imperial carriage halted north of Longxing. Zhongliang memorialized: "Shiregi's rebellion arose because Antong's provisions did not reach them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourteenth year, while the court was encamped north of Longxing, Zhongliang said, "Shiregi's rebellion stemmed from Antong's troops going without adequate rations.

sentences.zh: 今宿衛之士，日食一瓜，豈能充飢，竊有怨言矣。」

translations.literal: Now the palace guards eat but one melon a day — how can that fill their hunger? There are already private complaints."
translations.idiomatic: Today the palace guards receive only one melon a day — hardly enough to sustain them — and discontent is already spreading."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，笞主膳二人，俾均其食。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, flogged the two chief provisioners, and ordered rations to be distributed equally.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, had the two chief provisioners flogged, and ordered rations distributed fairly.

sentences.zh: 十五年三月，汴梁河清三百里，帝曰：「憲宗生，河清；

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifteenth year the Yellow River at Bianliang ran clear for three hundred li. The emperor said: "When Emperor Xianzong was born, the river ran clear;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifteenth year the Yellow River at Bianliang ran clear for three hundred li. The emperor said, "When Emperor Xianzong was born, the river ran clear;

sentences.zh: 朕生，河又清；

translations.literal: when I was born, the river ran clear again;
translations.idiomatic: when I was born, it ran clear again;

sentences.zh: 今河又清，何耶？」

translations.literal: now the river runs clear again — why?"
translations.idiomatic: and now it runs clear once more — what does this mean?"

sentences.zh: 忠良對曰：「應在皇太子宮矣。」

translations.literal: Zhongliang replied: "The omen applies to the Heir Apparent's palace."
translations.idiomatic: "The omen concerns the Heir Apparent," Zhongliang replied."

sentences.zh: 帝語符寶郎董文忠曰：「是不妄言，殆有徵也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the Keeper of Seals Dong Wenzhong: "This man does not speak idly — there is likely a sign in it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Dong Wenzhong, Keeper of the Imperial Seals, "He does not speak lightly — there may be something to this."

sentences.zh: 十八年，特命為太常丞。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was specially appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was specially appointed Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 少府為諸王昌童建宅於太廟南，忠良往僕其柱，少府奏之，帝問忠良，對曰：「太廟前豈諸王建宅所耶？」

translations.literal: The Palace Provisioner built a residence for Prince Changtong south of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Zhongliang went to lean against its pillars; the Provisioner reported this. The emperor questioned Zhongliang, who replied: "Before the Imperial Ancestral Temple — is that a place for princes to build residences?"
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Provisioner was building a mansion for Prince Changtong south of the Imperial Ancestral Temple. Zhongliang leaned against its pillars in protest. When the Provisioner reported this and the emperor questioned him, Zhongliang said, "Is the ground before the Imperial Ancestral Temple fit for a prince's residence?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: "You are right," the emperor said."

sentences.zh: 又奏曰：「太廟前無馳道，非禮也。」

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "Before the Imperial Ancestral Temple there is no imperial roadway — this is not according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "There is no imperial roadway before the temple — this violates ritual propriety."

sentences.zh: 即敕中書辟道。

translations.literal: An edict immediately ordered the Secretariat to open a roadway.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered the Secretariat to open one.

sentences.zh: 國製，十月上吉，有事於太廟。

translations.literal: By national custom, on an auspicious day in the upper part of the tenth month, sacrifices are performed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: By dynastic custom, sacrifices at the Imperial Ancestral Temple are held on an auspicious day early in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 或請牲不用牛，忠良奏曰：「梁武帝用面為犧牲，後如何耶？」

translations.literal: Some requested that sacrificial victims not use cattle. Zhongliang memorialized: "Emperor Wu of Liang used dough for sacrificial victims — what became of him afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed dispensing with cattle as sacrificial victims. Zhongliang objected, "Emperor Wu of Liang offered dough in place of livestock — and what became of his dynasty?"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His view was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 遷太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十年，將徵日本國，召忠良擇日出師，忠良奏曰：「僻陋海隅，何足勞天戈。」

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, when an expedition against Japan was planned, Zhongliang was summoned to choose the day for the army's departure. He memorialized: "A remote corner of the sea — why trouble the imperial arms?"
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, as an expedition against Japan was being planned, Zhongliang was asked to select an auspicious departure date. He urged, "Why waste the imperial armies on a remote island at the edge of the sea?"

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His advice was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，請建太社於朝右，建郊壇於國南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he requested building the Grand Earth Altar to the right of the court and the suburban altar south of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he petitioned to erect the Grand Earth Altar to the right of the palace and the suburban sacrifice altar south of the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄兼引進使。

translations.literal: Shortly he also served concurrently as Introducing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also appointed Introducing Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遷太常卿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，遷昭文館大學士、中奉大夫，兼太常太卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was transferred to Grand Academician of the Hall for the Diffusion of Literature and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, concurrently serving as Grand Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dade (1297) he became Grand Academician of the Hall for the Diffusion of Literature and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, while retaining his post as Grand Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十一年，成宗崩，阿忽台等持異謀，將以皇后教，祔成宗於廟。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Emperor Chengzong died; Ahutai and others held a divergent plot, intending to enshrine Chengzong in the temple by the empress's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Emperor Chengzong died. Ahutai and his faction plotted to install the deceased emperor in the ancestral temple by empress's decree rather than by proper succession ritual.

sentences.zh: 忠良爭曰：「嗣皇帝祔先帝於廟，禮也；

translations.literal: Zhongliang contended: "For the succeeding emperor to enshrine the former emperor in the temple is ritual propriety;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang protested, "It is proper ritual for the succeeding emperor to install his predecessor in the ancestral temple;

sentences.zh: 皇后教，非制也。」

translations.literal: an empress's command is not institutional precedent."
translations.idiomatic: an empress's decree is not established precedent."

sentences.zh: 阿忽台等怒曰：「制自天降耶？

translations.literal: Ahutai and others angrily said: "Does precedent fall from heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Ahutai's faction raged, "Do you think precedent falls from heaven?

sentences.zh: 汝不畏死，敢沮大事！」

translations.literal: You do not fear death — you dare obstruct a great affair!"
translations.idiomatic: You dare risk your life to block our plans!"

sentences.zh: 忠良竟不從。

translations.literal: Zhongliang ultimately would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang held firm and refused.

sentences.zh: 既而仁宗以太弟奉皇太后至自懷州，潛與密謀誅阿忽台等。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Renzong, as heir younger brother, escorted the Empress Dowager back from Huai Prefecture and secretly joined in plotting to execute Ahutai and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the future Emperor Renzong, as heir apparent, escorted the Empress Dowager back from Huai Prefecture and secretly conspired to execute Ahutai and his faction.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，進榮祿大夫、大司徒，賜銀印。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Zhongliang was advanced to Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and granted a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Zhongliang was promoted to Grand Master for Glorious Blessings and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and received a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，又進光祿大夫，領太常禮儀院事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was further advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and put in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong succeeded, he was further promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and placed in charge of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Ritual.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年正月卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Yanyou he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first month of the fourth year of Yanyou (1317), at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠守正佐運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封趙國公，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Loyalty, Upheld Rectitude, and Assisted the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, Grand Marshal with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, and Pillar of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous name Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Meritorious Minister Who Pushed Loyalty, Upheld Rectitude, and Assisted the Mandate, Grand Preceptor, and Pillar of the State with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with the posthumous name Zhongxian (Loyal and Dedicated).

sentences.zh: 子天澤，翰林侍講學士、嘉議大夫、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: His son Tianze served as Attendant Academician of the Hanlin Academy, Grand Master for Exalted Counsel, and Drafting Edicts and Compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tianze served as Attendant Academician of the Hanlin Academy, Grand Master for Exalted Counsel, drafter of edicts, and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 靳德進，其先潞州人，後徙大名。

translations.literal: Jin Dejin — his ancestors were from Luzhou; later the family moved to Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Dejin came from a family originally of Luzhou that later relocated to Daming.

sentences.zh: 祖璇，業儒。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xuan pursued Confucian studies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xuan was a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 父祥，師事陵川郝溫，兼善星曆。

translations.literal: His father Xiang studied under Hao Wen of Lingchuan and was also skilled in astronomy and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiang studied under Hao Wen of Lingchuan and was also accomplished in astronomy and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 金末兵亂，與母相失，母悲泣而盲，祥訪得之，舐其目，百日復明，人稱其孝。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin, amid military chaos, he was separated from his mother; she wept in grief until blind. Xiang searched and found her, licked her eyes, and after a hundred days her sight was restored — people praised his filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: During the chaos at the end of the Jin dynasty he was separated from his mother, who wept until she went blind. Xiang found her, licked her eyes in the ancient healing rite, and after a hundred days her sight returned — an act of filial devotion widely praised.

sentences.zh: 國初，玉出乾劉敏行省於燕，辟祥置幕下，佩以金符。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, when Yelü Chucai and Liu Min were regional commissioners in Yan, they recruited Xiang to their staff and bestowed a gold tally on him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty, when Yelü Chucai and Liu Min governed the Yan region, they took Xiang onto their staff and awarded him a gold tally of authority.

sentences.zh: 時籓帥得擅生殺，無辜者多賴祥以免。

translations.literal: At that time frontier commanders could arbitrarily decide life and death; many innocents owed their escape to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In those days frontier princes held the power of life and death, and many innocents were spared only through Xiang's intervention.

sentences.zh: 贈集賢大學士，諡安靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was granted Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, with the posthumous name Anjing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies with the posthumous name Anjing (Peaceful and Tranquil).

sentences.zh: 德進為人材辨，幼讀書，能通大義，父歿，益自刻勵，尤精於星曆之學。

translations.literal: Dejin was discerning in talent; from youth he read books and could grasp great principles. After his father's death he redoubled his self-discipline, especially mastering the study of astronomy and calendrics.
translations.idiomatic: Dejin was a man of keen discernment. He read widely from youth and grasped essential principles. After his father's death he applied himself with redoubled discipline, becoming especially expert in astronomy and calendrics.

sentences.zh: 世祖命太保秉忠選太史官屬，德進以選授天文、星曆、卜筮三科管勾，凡交蝕躔次、六氣侵沴，所言休咎輒應。

translations.literal: Shizu ordered Grand Preceptor Bingzhong to select staff for the Directorate of Astronomy; Dejin was chosen and appointed superintendent of the three sections of astronomy, calendrics, and divination. In all matters of eclipses, planetary positions, and the six qi in conflict — whatever he said of fortune or misfortune invariably came to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai ordered Liu Bingzhong to select staff for the Directorate of Astronomy. Dejin was chosen and made superintendent of its three divisions — astronomy, calendrics, and divination. Whether predicting eclipses, planetary movements, or atmospheric disturbances, his forecasts of fortune and misfortune invariably proved correct.

sentences.zh: 時因天象以進規諫，多所裨益。

translations.literal: At the time he used celestial phenomena to offer remonstrance and admonition, greatly benefiting the state.
translations.idiomatic: He often used celestial omens as occasions to offer remonstrance to the throne, to considerable benefit.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書監，掌司天事。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached Director of the Palace Library, in charge of astronomical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Director of the Palace Library, overseeing all astronomical affairs.

sentences.zh: 從征叛王乃顏，揆度日時，率中機會。

translations.literal: Accompanying the campaign against the rebel prince Nayan, in calculating days and times he generally hit the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against the rebel prince Nayan, his calculations of timing and auspicious moments proved consistently accurate.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲剿絕其黨，德進獨陳天道好生，請緩師以待其降。

translations.literal: The generals wished to exterminate his faction entirely; Dejin alone cited heaven's way of cherishing life and requested slowing the army to await their surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals wanted to annihilate Nayan's followers, Dejin alone appealed to heaven's preference for preserving life and urged them to hold back and await surrender.

sentences.zh: 俄奏言：「叛始由惑於妖言，遂謀不軌，宜括天下術士，設陰陽教官，使訓學者，仍歲貢有成者一人。」

translations.literal: Shortly he memorialized: "The rebellion began from being deluded by demonic talk and thus plotting treason. It is fitting to gather occult specialists throughout the realm, establish Yin-Yang instruction officials to train students, and each year present one who has achieved mastery."
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized, "This rebellion began with men led astray by occult prophecy. We should register diviners throughout the realm, appoint Yin-Yang instructors to train students properly, and each year present one accomplished graduate to the court."

sentences.zh: 帝從之，遂著為令。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and it was established as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the policy was enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 張康，字汝安，號明遠，潭州湘潭人。

translations.literal: Zhang Kang, courtesy name Ru'an, style name Mingyuan, was a native of Xiangtan in Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kang, styled Ru'an and known as Mingyuan, came from Xiangtan in Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖安厚，父世英。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Anhou, and his father was Shiying.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was named Anhou and his father was named Shiying.

sentences.zh: 康早孤力學，旁通術數。

translations.literal: Kang lost his father early and studied diligently, broadly mastering numerology and the occult arts.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Kang devoted himself to study and became widely versed in divination and numerology.

sentences.zh: 宋呂文德、江万裡、留夢炎皆推重之，辟置幕下。

translations.literal: Under the Song, Lü Wende, Jiang Wanli, and Liu Mengyan all esteemed him highly and recruited him into their staffs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Song, Lü Wende, Jiang Wanli, and Liu Mengyan all held him in high regard and brought him onto their staffs.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，隱衡山。

translations.literal: When the Song fell, he went into seclusion on Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song dynasty fell, he withdrew to live in seclusion on Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，世祖遣中丞崔彧祀南嶽，就訪隱逸。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, the Shizu emperor dispatched Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu to sacrifice at the Southern Peak and, while there, to seek out recluses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277, Emperor Shizu sent Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu to perform rites at Mount Heng and to inquire after reclusive worthies on the way.

sentences.zh: 彧兄湖南行省參政崔斌言康隱衡山，學通天文地理。

translations.literal: Yu's elder brother Cui Bin, Vice Administrator of the Hunan Branch Secretariat, reported that Kang was hiding on Mount Heng and that his learning embraced astronomy and geography.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's elder brother Cui Bin, a vice administrator of the Hunan Branch Secretariat, told him that Kang was living in seclusion on Mount Heng and was versed in astronomy and geography.

sentences.zh: 彧還，具以聞，遣使召康，與斌偕至京師。

translations.literal: When Yu returned, he reported everything in full, and an envoy was sent to summon Kang; together with Bin he arrived at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, Yu reported this in full to the court, which dispatched an envoy to summon Kang; he and Bin traveled together to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十五年夏四月，至上都見帝，親試所學，大驗，授著作佐郎，仍以內嬪松夫人妻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer in the fifteenth year, he went to the Upper Capital to see the emperor; his learning was tested in person and proved greatly accurate; he was appointed Assistant Compiler and moreover given Lady Song of the inner palace as his wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer 1278 he appeared before the emperor at Shangdu; the emperor personally tested his skills and found them remarkably accurate. He was appointed Assistant Compiler, and the court also gave him Lady Song of the inner palace in marriage.

sentences.zh: 凡召對，禮遇殊厚，呼以明遠而不名。

translations.literal: Whenever he was summoned for audience, the courtesy shown was exceptionally generous; he was addressed as Mingyuan rather than by name.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was summoned to audience, he received exceptional honors; the emperor called him Mingyuan and never used his personal name.

sentences.zh: 嘗面諭：凡有所問，使極言之。

translations.literal: Once the emperor personally instructed him: "Whatever you are asked, speak to the utmost."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told him face to face, "When I question you about anything, speak your mind fully."

sentences.zh: 十八年，康上奏：「歲壬午，太一理艮宮，主大將客、參將囚，直符治事，正屬燕分。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Kang memorialized: "In the year renpwu, Taiyi governs the Gen Palace; the Grand General is guest, the Deputy General is imprisoned, and the Direct Talisman handles affairs — this directly corresponds to the Yan region.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 Kang submitted a memorial: "In the year renpwu, Taiyi occupies the Gen Palace, with the Grand General as guest, the Deputy General imprisoned, and the Direct Talisman in charge of affairs — precisely the sphere of the Yan region.

sentences.zh: 明年春，京城當有盜兵，事干將相。」

translations.literal: Next spring, the capital will have bandit-soldiers; the affair will involve generals and ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Next spring the capital will see armed rebels, and the affair will touch generals and chief ministers."

sentences.zh: 十九年三月，盜果起京師，殺阿合馬等。

translations.literal: In the third month of the nineteenth year, bandits indeed rose in the capital and killed Ahmad and others.
translations.idiomatic: In March 1282 rebels did arise in the capital and killed Ahmad and others.

sentences.zh: 帝欲徵日本，命康以太一推之，康奏曰：「南國甫定，民力未蘇，且今年太一無算，舉兵不利。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to campaign against Japan and ordered Kang to calculate by Taiyi; Kang memorialized, saying: "The southern lands have only just been pacified and the people's strength has not yet recovered; moreover, this year Taiyi is unfathomable — raising troops would be unpropitious."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned a campaign against Japan, he had Kang read the Taiyi charts. Kang replied, "The south has only just been subdued and the people are not yet restored. This year Taiyi offers no favorable reckoning; to mobilize now would be ill-advised."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜太史院錢，分千貫以與康，不受，眾服其廉。

translations.literal: Once funds were granted to the Astrological Academy and a share of one thousand strings of cash was given to Kang; he did not accept it, and the multitude admired his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when the Astrological Academy received a grant, Kang was offered a thousand strings of cash; he refused, and everyone respected him for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 久之，乞歸田裡，優詔不許，遷奉直大夫、秘書監丞。

translations.literal: After a long time he requested to return to his fields and village; an indulgent edict did not permit this; he was transferred to Grand Master for Fostering Integrity and Deputy Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he asked to retire to his home village, but an exceptional edict denied the request and he was promoted to Grand Master for Fostering Integrity and Deputy Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 年六十五卒。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 子天祐。

translations.literal: His son was Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: He left a son named Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 李杲，字明之，鎮人也，世以貲雄鄉里。

translations.literal: Li Gao, courtesy name Mingzhi, was a man of Zhen; generation after generation his family was wealthy and dominated the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao, styled Mingzhi, came from Zhen; his family had been wealthy and prominent in the region for generations.

sentences.zh: 杲幼歲好醫藥，時易人張元素以醫名燕趙間，杲捐千金從之學，不數年，盡傳其業。

translations.literal: Gao from youth loved medicine and pharmacy; at the time Zhang Yuansu of Yi was famed for medicine between Yan and Zhao; Gao contributed a thousand gold to study under him, and in not many years fully received his profession.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Gao loved medicine. Zhang Yuansu of Yi was then the most celebrated physician in the Yan-Zhao region; Gao paid a thousand in gold to study under him and within a few years had mastered his entire art.

sentences.zh: 家既富厚，無事於技，操有餘以自重，人不敢以醫名之。

translations.literal: His family being already rich and substantial, he had no need to rely on his skill for a living; he carried himself with reserve from his surplus, and people did not dare address him as a physician by profession.
translations.idiomatic: His family was already wealthy, so he had no need to practice medicine for a living; secure in his means, he carried himself with reserve, and people did not dare treat him as a common physician.

sentences.zh: 大夫士或病其資性高謇，少所降屈，非危急之疾，不敢謁也。

translations.literal: Great officers and scholar-gentlemen sometimes took issue with his high and blunt temperament and that he seldom lowered himself; unless the illness was urgent and critical, they did not dare to call on him.
translations.idiomatic: Some gentlemen found his proud, uncompromising temperament off-putting; unless the case was truly dire, they hesitated to seek him out.

sentences.zh: 其學於傷寒、癰疽、眼目病為尤長。

translations.literal: In his learning, cold-damage disorders, abscesses and sores, and eye diseases were especially his strengths.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially masterful in treating cold-damage fevers, abscesses, and eye disorders.

sentences.zh: 北京人王善甫，為京兆酒官，病小便不利，目睛凸出，腹脹如鼓，膝以上堅硬欲裂，飲食且不下，甘淡滲洩之藥皆不效。

translations.literal: Wang Shanpu of Beijing, who served as wine officer of Jingzhao, was ill with difficult urination; his eyeballs protruded, his belly swelled like a drum, the area above his knees was hard as if about to split, he could hardly keep down food or drink, and sweet-bland draining medicines all failed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shanpu of Beijing, a wine officer in the Jingzhao region, suffered from urinary retention. His eyes bulged, his abdomen swelled drum-tight, and the flesh above his knees hardened as if it might split. He could barely eat or drink, and every sweet, bland diuretic the other physicians tried failed.

sentences.zh: 杲謂眾醫曰：「疾深矣。

translations.literal: Gao said to the assembled physicians: "The disease is deep.
translations.idiomatic: Gao told the other physicians, "This illness is far advanced.

sentences.zh: 《內經》有之：膀胱者，津液之府，必氣化乃出焉。

translations.literal: The Inner Canon has it: "The bladder is the treasury of fluids; only when qi transforms can they be discharged."
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Canon says, "The bladder is the storehouse of fluids; they can be released only when qi transforms them."

sentences.zh: 今用滲洩之劑而病益甚者，是氣不化也。

translations.literal: Now using draining-dispersing formulas yet the disease grows worse — this is that qi is not transforming.
translations.idiomatic: If draining formulas are used and the illness only worsens, it means the qi is failing to transform.

sentences.zh: 啟玄子云：'無陽者陰無以生，無陰者陽無以化。

translations.literal: Qixuanzi said: 'Where there is no yang, yin has nothing by which to be generated; where there is no yin, yang has nothing by which to transform.'
translations.idiomatic: Qixuanzi wrote, "Without yang, yin cannot be generated; without yin, yang cannot transform."

sentences.zh: '甘淡滲洩皆陽藥，獨陽無陰，其欲化得乎？」

translations.literal: Sweet-bland draining-dispersing medicines are all yang drugs; yang alone without yin — can transformation be achieved?'
translations.idiomatic: Sweet, bland diuretics are all yang medicines. With yang alone and no yin, how can transformation occur?"

sentences.zh: 明日，以群陰之劑投，不再服而愈。

translations.literal: The next day he administered a formula of multiple yin agents; without needing a second dose, the patient recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he prescribed a compound of yin-natured medicines; the patient needed no second dose and recovered.

sentences.zh: 西台掾蕭君瑞，二月中病傷寒發熱，醫以白虎湯投之，病者面黑如墨，本證不復見，脈沉細，小便不禁。

translations.literal: Xiao Junrui, clerk of the Western Platform Secretariat, in the second month fell ill with cold-damage fever; physicians administered White Tiger Decoction; the patient's face turned black as ink, the original symptoms no longer appeared, the pulse was deep and fine, and he could not control urination.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Junrui, a clerk on the Western Platform, contracted a cold-damage fever in the second month. Physicians gave him White Tiger Decoction. His face turned ink-black, the original symptoms vanished, his pulse was deep and thready, and he lost control of urination.

sentences.zh: 杲初不知用何藥，及診之，曰：「此立夏前誤用白虎湯之過。

translations.literal: Gao at first did not know what medicine had been used; when he examined the patient, he said: "This is the error of having misused White Tiger Decoction before the Start of Summer.
translations.idiomatic: Gao did not at first know what medicine had been given, but on examining the patient he said, "This is the result of misusing White Tiger Decoction before the Start of Summer.

sentences.zh: 白虎湯大寒，非行經之藥，止能寒腑藏，不善用之，則傷寒本病隱曲於經絡之間。

translations.literal: White Tiger Decoction is extremely cold; it is not a medicine that travels the channels; it can only chill the bowels and viscera — if used improperly, the original cold-damage disease hides and curves within the channels and collaterals.
translations.idiomatic: White Tiger Decoction is intensely cold; it is not a channel-traveling medicine and can only chill the bowels and viscera. Used improperly, it drives the underlying cold-damage illness into hiding within the channels and collaterals.

sentences.zh: 或更以大熱之藥救之，以苦陰邪，則他證必起，非所以救白虎也。

translations.literal: If one then uses extremely hot medicines to rescue it, to subdue yin evil with bitterness, other symptoms will surely arise — this is not the way to remedy White Tiger.
translations.idiomatic: If one then tries to counter it with intensely hot medicines to suppress the yin pathogen, other symptoms will inevitably appear — that is not how to undo the harm of White Tiger Decoction.

sentences.zh: 有溫藥之昇陽行經者，吾用之。」

translations.literal: There are warm medicines that raise yang and travel the channels — I shall use them."
translations.idiomatic: I will use warm medicines that lift yang and move through the channels."

sentences.zh: 有難者曰： 「白虎大寒，非大熱何以救，君之治奈何？」

translations.literal: A challenger said: "White Tiger is extremely cold — without great heat how can it be rescued? What is your treatment?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone objected, "White Tiger Decoction is intensely cold — how can anything but great heat remedy that? What is your approach?"

sentences.zh: 杲曰：「病隱於經絡間，陽不升則經不行，經行而本證見矣。

translations.literal: Gao said: "The disease is hidden in the channels and collaterals; if yang does not rise, the channels cannot move; once the channels move, the original symptoms will appear.
translations.idiomatic: Gao replied, "The illness is lodged in the channels and collaterals. If yang does not rise, the channels cannot function; once the channels move again, the original symptoms will reappear.

sentences.zh: 本證又何難焉。」

translations.literal: The original symptoms — what difficulty is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Then treating the original illness will be straightforward."

sentences.zh: 果如其言而愈。

translations.literal: It turned out exactly as he said, and the patient recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Events unfolded exactly as he had predicted, and the patient recovered.

sentences.zh: 魏邦彥之妻，目翳暴生，從下而上，其色綠，腫痛不可忍。

translations.literal: The wife of Wei Bangyan suddenly developed eye film, rising from below upward; its color was green, and the swelling and pain were unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Wei Bangyan suddenly developed a film over her eye, spreading upward from below. It was green in color, and the swelling and pain were unbearable.

sentences.zh: 杲云：「翳從下而上，病從陽明來也。

translations.literal: Gao said: "The film rises from below upward — the disease comes from Yangming.
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "A film rising from below means the illness originates in the Yangming channel.

sentences.zh: 綠非五色之正，殆肺與腎合而為病邪。」

translations.literal: Green is not one of the proper five colors — perhaps the lung and kidney have combined to form the disease."
translations.idiomatic: Green is not one of the five standard colors; this likely means the lung and kidney pathologies have joined together."

sentences.zh: 乃瀉肺腎之邪，而以入陽明之藥為之使。

translations.literal: He then purged the evil of lung and kidney and used medicines entering Yangming as envoys.
translations.idiomatic: He purged the pathogenic influences in the lung and kidney and used medicines that enter the Yangming channel as guides.

sentences.zh: 既效矣，而他日病復作者三，其所從來之經，與翳色各異。

translations.literal: Once it took effect, yet on other days the disease recurred three times; the channels from which it came and the color of the film each differed.
translations.idiomatic: The treatment worked, but the condition recurred three times on later days, each time arising from a different channel and showing a different color in the film.

sentences.zh: 乃曰：「諸脈皆屬於目，脈病則目從之。

translations.literal: He then said: "All channels belong to the eye; when the channels are diseased, the eye follows them.
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "All the channels connect to the eyes; when a channel is diseased, the eye reflects it.

sentences.zh: 此必經絡不調，經不調，則目病未已也。」

translations.literal: This must be that the channels and collaterals are not regulated; if the channels are not regulated, the eye disease will not yet end."
translations.idiomatic: The channels and collaterals must be out of balance; until they are regulated, the eye disorder will not truly end."

sentences.zh: 問之果然，因如所論而治之，疾遂不作。

translations.literal: On inquiry it was indeed so; he therefore treated according to his analysis, and the disease then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry confirmed his diagnosis; he treated accordingly, and the illness never returned.

sentences.zh: 馮叔獻之侄櫟，年十五六，病傷寒，目赤而頓渴，脈七八至，醫欲以承氣湯下之，已煮藥，而杲適從外來，馮告之故。

translations.literal: Li, nephew of Feng Shuxian, aged fifteen or sixteen, was ill with cold-damage; his eyes were red and he was suddenly thirsty; his pulse came seven or eight times to the breath; physicians wished to purge him with Order-the-Qi Decoction; the medicine was already being boiled when Gao happened to come from outside, and Feng told him what had happened.
translations.idiomatic: Li, a nephew of Feng Shuxian, was fifteen or sixteen and suffering from cold-damage fever. His eyes were red and he was suddenly ravenous with thirst; his pulse raced seven or eight beats to the breath. Physicians were about to purge him with Order-the-Qi Decoction and had already begun boiling the medicine when Gao arrived from outside and Feng told him what was happening.

sentences.zh: 杲切脈，大駭曰：「幾殺此兒。

translations.literal: Gao felt the pulse and, greatly alarmed, said: "You nearly killed this boy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao took the pulse and cried out in alarm, "You almost killed this boy.

sentences.zh: 《內經》有言：'在脈，諸數為熱，諸遲為寒。

translations.literal: The Inner Canon has a saying: 'In the pulse, all rapid [pulses] are heat, all slow [pulses] are cold.'
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Canon says, "Among pulses, rapid ones indicate heat and slow ones indicate cold."

sentences.zh: '今脈八九至，是熱極也。

translations.literal: Now the pulse comes eight or nine times — this is heat at the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this pulse comes eight or nine times to the breath — that is heat pushed to the limit.

sentences.zh: 而《會要大論》云：'病有脈從而病反者何也？

translations.literal: Yet the "Comprehensive Treatise on the Essentials" says: 'When the disease has a pulse that conforms yet the disease is contrary — what is this?'
translations.idiomatic: But the Comprehensive Treatise on the Essentials asks, "When the pulse and the disease seem to agree yet the illness runs contrary, what does that mean?"

sentences.zh: 脈至而從，按之不鼓，諸陽皆然。

translations.literal: The pulse comes and conforms, yet when pressed it does not surge — all yang [signs] are like this.
translations.idiomatic: The pulse is rapid and seems to conform, yet when pressed it does not surge — that is true of all yang signs.

sentences.zh: '此傳而為陰證矣。

translations.literal: This has transformed into a yin syndrome.
translations.idiomatic: This has already transformed into a yin syndrome.

sentences.zh: 令持姜、附來，吾當以熱因寒用法處之。」

translations.literal: Have ginger and aconite brought; I shall treat it by the method of using heat because of cold."
translations.idiomatic: Bring ginger and aconite — I will treat this by the method of applying heat in response to cold."

sentences.zh: 藥未就而病者爪甲變，頓服者八​​兩，汗尋出而愈。

translations.literal: Before the medicine was ready the patient's fingernails changed color; he took eight taels at once, and sweat soon came forth and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Before the decoction was finished the patient's fingernails changed color. He took eight taels in one dose, sweat broke out shortly afterward, and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 陝帥郭巨濟病偏枯，二指著足底不能伸，杲以長針刺骫中，深至骨而不知痛，出血一二升，其色如墨，又且謬刺之。

translations.literal: Guo Juji, military commander of Shaan, was ill with hemiplegia; two fingers rested on the sole of the foot and could not extend; Gao used a long needle to puncture Weizhong, deep to the bone without the patient feeling pain, and blood flowed one or two sheng, its color like ink; he also needled elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Juji, commander in Shaan, suffered from hemiplegia; two fingers lay pressed against the sole of his foot and would not straighten. Gao drove a long needle into Weizhong, deep to the bone without causing pain, and one or two sheng of blood flowed out, black as ink. He needled other points as well.

sentences.zh: 如此者六七，服藥三月，病良已。

translations.literal: He did this six or seven times; after three months of taking medicine, the disease was fully cured.
translations.idiomatic: He repeated this six or seven times; after three months of medication the illness was completely cured.

sentences.zh: 裴擇之妻病寒熱，月事不至者數年，已喘嗽矣。

translations.literal: The wife of Pei Ze was ill with alternating chills and fever; her monthly period had not come for several years, and she was already coughing with wheezing.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Pei Ze suffered from alternating chills and fever; her menses had ceased for several years, and she was already coughing and wheezing.

sentences.zh: 醫者率以蛤蚧、桂、附之藥投之，杲曰：「不然，夫病陰為陽所搏，溫劑太過，故無益而反害。

translations.literal: Physicians generally administered medicines of gecko, cinnamon, and aconite; Gao said: "Not so — the disease is yin struck by yang; warm formulas are excessive, hence they bring no benefit but rather harm.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians had been treating her with gecko, cinnamon, and aconite. Gao said, "No — her yin has been overwhelmed by yang. Warm formulas are too strong here; they do no good and only make matters worse.

sentences.zh: 投以寒血之藥，則經行矣。」

translations.literal: Administer medicines of cold blood, and the menses will flow."
translations.idiomatic: Give her cold-natured blood-moving medicines, and her menses will return."

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: Before long it was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: It happened exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 杲之設施多類此。

translations.literal: Gao's treatments were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Most of Gao's cures followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 當時之人，皆以神醫目之。

translations.literal: People of the time all regarded him as a divine physician.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries regarded him as a miraculous physician.

sentences.zh: 所著書，今多傳於世云。

translations.literal: The books he authored are now widely transmitted in the world, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Many of the books he wrote are still widely circulated today.

sentences.zh: 孫威，渾源人。

translations.literal: Sun Wei was a man of Hunyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wei came from Hunyuan.

sentences.zh: 幼沉鷙，有巧思。

translations.literal: From youth he was deep and shrewd, with ingenious ideas.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was steady and sharp-minded, with a gift for invention.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐間，應募為兵，以驍勇稱。

translations.literal: During the Zhenyou era of Jin, he answered the call to serve as a soldier and was famed for fierce bravery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin dynasty's Zhenyou era he enlisted as a soldier and earned a reputation for fierce courage.

sentences.zh: 及雲中來附，守帥表授義軍千戶，從軍攻潞州，破鳳翔，皆有功。

translations.literal: When he came from Yunzhong to submit, the defending commander memorialized to appoint him chiliarch of the Righteous Army; he followed the army in attacking Luz Prefecture and breaking Fengxiang, achieving merit in each.
translations.idiomatic: When he came from Yunzhong to join the Mongols, the local commander recommended him as chiliarch of a volunteer unit. He campaigned at Luz Prefecture and helped capture Fengxiang, distinguishing himself in both.

sentences.zh: 善為甲，嘗以意制蹄筋翎根鎧以獻，太祖親射之，不能徹，大悅。

translations.literal: He was skilled at making armor; once by his own design he made armor of hoof-tendon and feather-root and presented it; the Taizu emperor personally shot at it and could not pierce it — he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He was a master armorer. Once he devised and presented a suit made from hoof sinew and feather shafts. Taizu shot at it himself and could not pierce it; he was delighted.

sentences.zh: 賜名也可兀蘭，佩以金符，授順天安平懷州河南平陽諸路工匠都總管。

translations.literal: He was granted the name Keyewulan, invested with a gold tally, and appointed Grand Supervisor of Artisans for the circuits of Shuntian, Anping, Huaizhou, Henan, and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the name Keyewulan, awarded a gold tally, and appointed Grand Supervisor of Artisans for Shuntian, Anping, Huaizhou, Henan, Pingyang, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 從攻邠、乾，突戰不避矢石，帝勞之曰：「汝縱不自愛，獨不為吾甲胄計乎！」

translations.literal: Following the attack on Bin and Qian, in sudden assaults he did not avoid arrows and stones; the emperor consoled him, saying: "Even if you do not cherish yourself, will you not consider my armor?"
translations.idiomatic: During campaigns at Bin and Qian he charged into battle without flinching from arrows and stones. The emperor remonstrated with him, saying, "Even if you care nothing for your own life, have you no regard for the armor I depend on?"

sentences.zh: 因命諸將衣其甲者問曰：「汝等知所愛重否？」

translations.literal: He then ordered the generals wearing his armor and asked: "Do you know what you should cherish?"
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the generals who wore Wei's armor and asked, "Do you know what you ought to value?"

sentences.zh: 諸將對，皆失旨意。

translations.literal: The generals replied, all missing the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The generals answered, but none grasped what he meant.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「能捍蔽爾輩以與我國家立功者，非威之甲耶！

translations.literal: Taizong said: "What can shield and cover you so that you may render merit to our state — is it not Wei's armor!
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "What shields you and lets you serve the state — is it not Wei's armor?

sentences.zh: 而爾輩言不及此，何也？」

translations.literal: Yet your words do not reach this — why?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet none of you said as much — why not?"

sentences.zh: 復以錦衣賜威。

translations.literal: He again bestowed brocade robes on Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He then rewarded Wei with brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 每從戰伐，恐民有橫被屠戮者，輒以搜簡工匠為言，而全活之。

translations.literal: Whenever he followed campaigns, fearing that common people might be indiscriminately slaughtered, he would speak of searching out and selecting artisans and thereby preserve their lives.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign he feared that civilians might be slaughtered indiscriminately; he would plead to have craftsmen rounded up and selected, thereby saving many lives.

sentences.zh: 歲庚子，卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the year gengzi he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the gengzi year at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，贈中奉大夫、武備院使、神川郡公，諡忠惠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhida he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Attending Affairs, Commissioner of the Armory Court, and Duke of Shenchuan, with the posthumous title Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 he was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Attending Affairs, Commissioner of the Armory Court, and Duke of Shenchuan, with the posthumous name Loyal and Gracious.

sentences.zh: 子拱，為監察御史，後襲順天安平懷州河南等路甲匠都總管。

translations.literal: His son Gong served as Investigating Censor and later inherited the post of Grand Supervisor of Armor Artisans for the circuits of Shuntian, Anping, Huaizhou, Henan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong served as an investigating censor and later inherited the post of Grand Supervisor of Armor Artisans for Shuntian, Anping, Huaizhou, Henan, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 巧思如其父，嘗制甲二百八十襲以獻。

translations.literal: His ingenuity matched his father's; once he made two hundred eighty suits of armor and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's ingenuity and once presented two hundred eighty suits of armor to the court.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，別制疊盾，其制，張則為盾，斂則合而易持。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan he separately devised folding shields; in their design, when spread they served as shields, when folded they closed together and were easy to carry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 he invented a folding shield: spread open it served as a shield, folded shut it was compact and easy to carry.

sentences.zh: 世祖以為古所未有，賜以幣帛。

translations.literal: Shizu considered that antiquity had never had such a thing and bestowed silks and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu declared that nothing like it had existed in antiquity and rewarded him with silks and cloth.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏南征，以甲胄不足，詔諸路集匠民分制。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan campaigned south, because armor was insufficient, an edict ordered the circuits to gather artisan households to manufacture it in shares.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Bayan marched south, armor ran short; the court ordered every circuit to mobilize craftsmen and divide production among them.

sentences.zh: 拱董順天、河間甲匠，先期畢工，且象虎豹異獸之形，各殊其制，皆稱旨。

translations.literal: Gong supervised the armor artisans of Shuntian and Hejian; they finished the work ahead of schedule, and moreover modeled tiger, leopard, and other exotic beasts, each with a distinct design — all met with approval.
translations.idiomatic: Gong oversaw the armor craftsmen of Shuntian and Hejian. They finished ahead of schedule and fashioned pieces in the shapes of tigers, leopards, and other exotic beasts, each with a unique design — all to the emperor's satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授保定路治中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed Administrative Assistant of Baoding Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was appointed administrative assistant of Baoding Circuit.

sentences.zh: 適歲饑，議開倉賑民，或曰：「宜請於朝。」

translations.literal: It happened to be a year of famine; they deliberated opening the granaries to relieve the people; someone said: "It is fitting to request permission from the court."
translations.idiomatic: That year brought famine, and officials debated opening the granaries to feed the people. Some said, "We should request permission from the court."

sentences.zh: 拱曰：「救荒事不可緩也，若得請而後發粟以賑之，則民餒死矣。

translations.literal: Gong said: "Relief in famine cannot be delayed; if one waits to obtain permission before issuing grain to relieve them, the people will starve to death.
translations.idiomatic: Gong replied, "Famine relief cannot wait. If we hold back grain until permission arrives, people will die of hunger.

sentences.zh: 苟見罪，吾自任之。」

translations.literal: If I am punished, I shall bear it myself."
translations.idiomatic: If I am punished for this, I will accept the blame myself."

sentences.zh: 遂發粟四千五百石以賑饑民。

translations.literal: He then issued four thousand five hundred shi of grain to relieve the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately released four thousand five hundred shi of grain to feed the starving population.

sentences.zh: 高陽土豪據沙河橋取行者錢，人以為病，拱執而罪之。

translations.literal: A local strongman of Gaoyang held Shahe Bridge and took money from travelers; people regarded this as a plague; Gong seized him and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: A local bully in Gaoyang controlled Shahe Bridge and extorted tolls from travelers, a grievance widely resented. Gong arrested him and punished him.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，除武備少卿，遷大都路軍器人匠總管，升工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Armory Court, transferred to Grand Supervisor of Military Equipment and Artisan Households of Dadu Circuit, and promoted to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 he was made Vice Commissioner of the Armory Court, then transferred to Grand Supervisor of Military Equipment and Artisan Households in Dadu, and promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，典朝會供給，賜銀百兩、織紋段五十匹、帛二十五匹、鈔萬貫。

translations.literal: When Chengzong ascended the throne, he managed supplies for court assemblies and was granted one hundred taels of silver, fifty bolts of brocade, twenty-five bolts of silk, and ten thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chengzong took the throne, Gong managed provisions for court assemblies and was rewarded with a hundred taels of silver, fifty bolts of brocade, twenty-five bolts of silk, and ten thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 元貞二年，授大同路總管，兼府尹。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanzhen he was appointed Prefect of Datong Circuit, concurrently serving as Prefectural Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1296 he was appointed prefect of Datong Circuit, serving concurrently as prefectural governor.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，遷兩浙都轉運使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade he was transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Two Zhe Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1301 he was transferred to Commissioner of Transport for the Two Zhe region.

sentences.zh: 鹽課舊二十五萬引，歲不能足，拱至增五萬引，遂為定額。

translations.literal: The salt levy had formerly been two hundred fifty thousand yin; each year it could not be filled; when Gong arrived he increased it by fifty thousand yin, and it then became the fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: The salt quota had stood at two hundred fifty thousand yin, but collections routinely fell short. Under Gong it rose by fifty thousand yin and that figure became the fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 九年，改益都路總管，兼府尹，仍出內府弓矢寶刀賜之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Prefect of Yidu Circuit, concurrently serving as Prefectural Governor, and moreover the inner palace issued bows, arrows, and precious swords as gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 he was reassigned as prefect of Yidu Circuit, again serving concurrently as prefectural governor, and the inner palace bestowed bows, arrows, and treasured swords upon him.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 贈大司農、神川郡公，諡文莊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Minister of Agriculture, made Duke of Shenchuan Commandery, and given the posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Minister of Agriculture and Duke of Shenchuan, with the posthumous name Cultured and Upright.

sentences.zh: 阿老瓦丁，回回氏，西域木發里人也。

translations.literal: Ala al-Din was of the Hui Muslim people; he was a native of Mayafarikin in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Ala al-Din was a Muslim from Mayafarikin in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，世祖遣使砲匠於宗王阿不哥，王以阿老瓦丁、亦思馬因應詔，二人舉家馳驛至京師，給以官舍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan, Shizu sent envoys to seek artillery craftsmen from the Prince of the Blood Abagha. The prince offered Ala al-Din and Ismail in response to the imperial summons; the two men brought their whole families posthaste by relay station to the capital, where official residences were provided.
translations.idiomatic: In 1271 Emperor Shizu sent envoys to Prince Abagha seeking artillery craftsmen. The prince dispatched Ala al-Din and Ismail in answer to the imperial summons; both men rushed their entire households by relay to the capital, where the court lodged them in official residences.

sentences.zh: 首造大砲豎於五門前，帝命試之，各賜衣段。

translations.literal: They first built great cannons and erected them before the Five Gates. The emperor ordered them tested and rewarded each with bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They built great cannons first and set them up before the Five Gates. The emperor ordered trials, then rewarded each man with bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 十一年，國兵渡江，平章阿里海牙遣使求砲手匠，命阿老瓦丁往，破潭州、靜江等郡，悉賴其力。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the national army crossed the Yangtze. Pingzhang Alihaiya sent envoys requesting cannon masters and craftsmen; Ala al-Din was ordered to go. The capture of Tanzhou, Jingjiang, and other commanderies all depended on his strength.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274, as the imperial army crossed the Yangtze, Pingzhang Alihaiya sent for cannon masters and craftsmen and dispatched Ala al-Din. The fall of Tanzhou, Jingjiang, and other commanderies owed everything to his skill.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授宣武將軍、管軍總管。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was appointed General Who Proclaims Martiality and Commander-in-Chief Who Manages Troops.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was made General Who Proclaims Martiality and commander-in-chief of troops under his charge.

sentences.zh: 十七年，陛見，賜鈔五千貫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he had an audience with the emperor and was granted five thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In 1280 he was received in audience and granted five thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命屯田於南京。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was ordered to establish military colonies at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he was ordered to establish military colonies at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，樞密院奉旨，改元帥府為回回砲手軍匠上萬戶府，以阿老瓦丁為副萬戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, on orders from the Privy Council, the Marshal's Office was renamed the Upper Myriarchate of Muslim Artillerymen and Military Craftsmen; Ala al-Din was made Deputy Myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 the Privy Council, acting on imperial orders, reorganized the marshal's office as the Upper Myriarchate of Muslim Artillerymen and Military Craftsmen and appointed Ala al-Din deputy myriarch.

sentences.zh: 大德四年告老。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade he requested retirement on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: In 1300 he retired on grounds of age.

sentences.zh: 子富謀只，襲副萬戶。

translations.literal: His son Fumouzhi inherited the post of Deputy Myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fumouzhi inherited the deputy myriarchate.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年卒，子馬哈馬沙襲。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Huangqing; his son Mahmushah inherited.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1312; his son Mahmushah succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 亦思馬因，回回氏，西域旭烈人也。

translations.literal: Ismail was of the Hui Muslim people; he was a native of Herat in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Ismail was a Muslim from Herat in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 善造砲，至元八年與阿老瓦丁至京師。

translations.literal: Skilled at building cannons, in the eighth year of Zhiyuan he came to the capital with Ala al-Din.
translations.idiomatic: A skilled cannon maker, he reached the capital with Ala al-Din in 1271.

sentences.zh: 十年，從國兵攻襄陽未下，亦思馬因相地勢，置砲於城東南隅，重一百五十斤，機發，聲震天地，所擊無不摧陷，入地七尺。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed the national army in the attack on Xiangyang, which had not yet fallen. Ismail surveyed the terrain and placed a cannon at the southeast corner of the city. The stone projectile weighed one hundred fifty jin. When the mechanism was released, the sound shook heaven and earth; whatever it struck was shattered and demolished, penetrating seven feet into the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In 1273 he joined the siege of Xiangyang, which still held out. Ismail studied the ground and emplaced a cannon at the city's southeast corner. The stone it hurled weighed one hundred fifty jin; when the mechanism fired, the blast shook heaven and earth. Nothing it struck escaped ruin, and the projectile buried itself seven feet deep.

sentences.zh: 宋安撫呂文煥懼，以城降。

translations.literal: Song pacification commissioner Lü Wenhuan was terrified and surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Song pacification commissioner Lü Wenhuan, terrified, surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 既而以功賜銀二百五十兩，命為回回砲手總管，佩虎符。

translations.literal: Then, for his merit, he was granted two hundred fifty taels of silver, appointed Grand Supervisor of Muslim Artillerymen, and invested with a tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he received two hundred fifty taels of silver, was appointed grand supervisor of Muslim artillerymen, and was invested with a tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十一年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in 1274.

sentences.zh: 子佈伯襲職。

translations.literal: His son Bucha inherited the office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bucha inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 時國兵渡江，宋兵陳於南岸，擁舟師迎戰，布伯於北岸豎砲以擊之，舟悉沉沒。

translations.literal: At the time the national army was crossing the Yangtze. Song troops deployed on the south bank with their fleet arrayed to meet battle. Bucha erected cannons on the north bank to strike them, and the boats all sank.
translations.idiomatic: While the imperial army was crossing the Yangtze, Song forces lined the south bank with their fleet ready for battle. Bucha set up cannons on the north bank and blasted them; every boat went down.

sentences.zh: 後每戰用之，皆有功。

translations.literal: Thereafter in every battle where they were used, they achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle thereafter where they were deployed, they won distinction.

sentences.zh: 十八年，佩三珠虎符，加鎮國上將軍、回回砲手都元帥。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was invested with a three-pearl tiger tally and promoted to General-in-Chief Who Stabilizes the State and Commander-in-Chief of Muslim Artillerymen.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he received a three-pearl tiger tally and was promoted to general-in-chief who stabilizes the state and commander-in-chief of Muslim artillerymen.

sentences.zh: 明年，改軍匠萬戶府萬戶。

translations.literal: The following year he was made Myriarch of the Myriarchate of Military Craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made myriarch of the Myriarchate of Military Craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部尚書，以弟亦不剌金為萬戶，佩元降虎符，官廣威將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Justice; his younger brother Ablaqin was made Myriarch, invested with a tiger tally of the Yuan dynasty, and given the rank of General of Broad Authority.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of justice; his younger brother Ablaqin was made myriarch, invested with an imperial tiger tally, and given the rank of general of broad authority.

sentences.zh: 布伯俄進通奉大夫、浙東道宣慰使，賜鈔二萬五千貫，俾養老焉。

translations.literal: Shortly Bucha was promoted to Grand Master for Appeasing Offerings and Pacification Commissioner for the Zhedong Circuit; he was granted twenty-five thousand strings of paper money with which to retire in comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Bucha was promoted to grand master for appeasing offerings and pacification commissioner for the Zhedong circuit, with twenty-five thousand strings of paper money to live out his old age.

sentences.zh: 子哈散，廕授昭信校尉、高郵府同知。

translations.literal: His son Hasan was granted office by hereditary privilege as Commandant of Illustrious Trust and Vice Prefect of Gaoyou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hasan received hereditary appointment as commandant of illustrious trust and vice prefect of Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 致和元年八月，樞密院檄亦不剌金所部軍匠至京師，賜鈔二千五百貫、金綺四端，與馬哈馬沙造砲。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Zhihe, the Privy Council summoned the military craftsmen under Ablaqin's command to the capital, granted them two thousand five hundred strings of paper money and four bolts of gold brocade, and had them build cannons together with Mahmushah.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of 1328 the Privy Council ordered the military craftsmen under Ablaqin to the capital, gave them two thousand five hundred strings of paper money and four bolts of gold brocade, and set them to building cannons with Mahmushah.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness in 1329.

sentences.zh: 子亞古襲。

translations.literal: His son Yagu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yagu succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 阿尼哥，尼波羅國人也，其國人稱之曰八魯布。

translations.literal: Anige was a native of the country of Nepal; the people of his country called him Balibu.
translations.idiomatic: Anige came from Nepal; his countrymen called him Balibu.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟異凡兒，稍長，誦習佛書，期年能曉其義。

translations.literal: As a child he was quick-witted and unlike ordinary boys. When he grew somewhat older he recited and studied Buddhist scriptures, and within a year could grasp their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was unusually bright and perceptive. When he grew older he studied Buddhist scriptures, and within a year he understood their meaning.

sentences.zh: 同學有為繪畫妝塑業者，讀《尺寸經》，阿尼哥一聞，即能記​​。

translations.literal: A fellow student who practiced painting, ornamentation, and sculpture read aloud from the Scripture of Measurements; Anige heard it once and could remember it entirely.
translations.idiomatic: A classmate who worked in painting, ornamentation, and sculpture was reading the Scripture of Measurements aloud; Anige heard it once and could recite it from memory.

sentences.zh: 長善畫塑，及鑄金為像。

translations.literal: When grown he excelled at painting and sculpture, and at casting gold into images.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he excelled at painting and sculpture and at casting images in gold.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，命帝師八合斯巴建黃金塔於吐蕃，尼波羅國選匠百人往成之，得八十人，求部送之人未得。
