translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, Imperial Preceptor Phagpa was ordered to build a golden pagoda in Tibet. The country of Nepal selected one hundred craftsmen to go and complete it; eighty were obtained, but the escort to convey them had not yet been found.
translations.idiomatic: In 1260 Imperial Preceptor Phagpa was ordered to build a golden pagoda in Tibet. Nepal selected one hundred craftsmen for the work; eighty were found, but no escort had yet been secured to convey them.

sentences.zh: 阿尼哥年十七，請行，眾以其幼，難之。

translations.literal: Anige was seventeen years old and requested to go; the others, taking him for too young, objected.
translations.idiomatic: Anige was seventeen and volunteered to go, but the others objected that he was too young.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「年幼心不幼也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Though young in years, my heart is not young."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I may be young in years, but my heart is not young."

sentences.zh: 乃遣之。

translations.literal: He was then dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: So he was sent.

sentences.zh: 帝師一見奇之，命監其役。

translations.literal: At first sight the Imperial Preceptor was struck by him and ordered him to oversee the labor.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Preceptor was astonished at first sight and put him in charge of the work.

sentences.zh: 明年，塔成，請歸，帝師勉以入朝，乃祝髮受具為弟子，從帝師入見。

translations.literal: The following year, when the pagoda was completed, he requested to return home. The Imperial Preceptor urged him to enter court audience; he then had his head tonsured and received the full precepts as a disciple, and accompanied the Imperial Preceptor to an audience.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the pagoda was finished, he asked to go home. Phagpa urged him to enter court instead; Anige had his head shaved, took full monastic vows as Phagpa's disciple, and accompanied him to an imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 帝視之久，問曰：「汝來大國，得無懼乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor looked at him for a long while and asked: "You have come to a great realm — are you not afraid?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor studied him for a long time and asked, "You have come to a great empire — are you not afraid?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「聖人子育萬方，子至父前，何懼之有。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The sage nourishes all within the four seas. When a son comes before his father, what is there to fear?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The sage nourishes all under heaven. When a son stands before his father, what is there to fear?"

sentences.zh: 又問：「汝來何為？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked again: "For what have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "Why have you come?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣家西域，奉命造塔吐蕃，二載而成。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject's family is from the Western Regions. I was commanded to build a pagoda in Tibet, and it was completed in two years.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your subject's family is from the Western Regions. I was ordered to build a pagoda in Tibet, and finished it in two years.

sentences.zh: 見彼土兵難，民不堪命，願陛下安輯之，不遠萬里，為生靈而來耳。」

translations.literal: I saw that land afflicted by warfare and the people unable to bear their lot. I wish that Your Majesty would pacify and settle them. I have come not ten thousand li for my own sake, but for the sake of the living people."
translations.idiomatic: I saw that land torn by war and the people crushed under hardship. I beg Your Majesty to pacify them. I have traveled ten thousand li not for myself, but for the sake of the people."

sentences.zh: 又問：「汝何所能？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "What are you capable of?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "What can you do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣以心為師，頗知畫塑鑄金之藝。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject takes the heart as his teacher and is fairly versed in the arts of painting, sculpture, and casting in gold."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your subject takes the heart as his teacher and is well versed in painting, sculpture, and casting in gold."

sentences.zh: 帝命取明堂針灸銅像示之曰：「此宣撫王楫使宋時所進，歲久闕壞，無能修完之者，汝能新之乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the bronze acupuncture figure from the Hall of Brightness brought forth and shown to him, saying: "This was presented when Commissioner Wang Ji was sent to the Song; after many years it has fallen into disrepair, and no one can restore it. Can you make it new?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the bronze acupuncture figure from the Hall of Brightness brought out and said, "This was presented when Commissioner Wang Ji was sent to the Song. After many years it has broken and no one can repair it. Can you make it anew?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣雖未嘗為此，請試之。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject has never done this before, but he requests to attempt it."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your subject has never done this, but I beg leave to try."

sentences.zh: 至元二年，新像成，關鬲脈絡皆備，金工歎其天巧，莫不愧服。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan the new figure was completed; the joints, openings, and meridian lines were all complete. Metalworkers marveled at its heaven-sent ingenuity; none failed to acknowledge defeat with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In 1265 the new figure was finished, with every joint, opening, and meridian line in place. Metalworkers marveled at its heaven-sent skill; none who saw it failed to acknowledge his mastery.

sentences.zh: 凡兩京寺觀之像，多出其手。

translations.literal: Most of the images in the temples and monasteries of the two capitals came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the images in the temples and monasteries of the two capitals were his work.

sentences.zh: 為七寶鑌鐵法輪，車駕行幸，用以前導。

translations.literal: He made a dharma wheel of seven treasures in Damascus steel; when the imperial carriage went on progress, it was used to lead the way.
translations.idiomatic: He made a seven-jeweled dharma wheel of Damascus steel that led the way whenever the imperial carriage went on progress.

sentences.zh: 原廟列聖御容，織錦為之，圖畫弗及也。

translations.literal: The imperial portraits of successive sages in the Original Ancestral Temple were made in woven brocade; painted images could not compare.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial portraits of successive emperors in the Original Ancestral Temple were rendered in woven brocade — beyond anything painting could achieve.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，始授人匠總管，銀章虎符。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan he was first appointed Grand Supervisor of Artisan Households and invested with a silver seal and tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In 1273 he was first appointed grand supervisor of artisan households and invested with a silver seal and tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 十五年，有詔返初服，授光祿大夫，大司徒，領將作院事，寵遇賞賜，無與為比。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict restored him to lay dress; he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor, and placed in charge of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. Favor, treatment, and rewards — none could be his equal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 an edict restored him to lay dress; he was made grand master for splendid happiness and grand preceptor and placed in charge of the Directorate of Palace Buildings. In favor, rank, and reward none could compare with him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太師、開府儀同三司、涼國公、上柱國，諡敏慧。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor, Grand Master with the Privilege of an Office Equal to the Three Excellencies, Duke of the State of Liang, and Pillar of State, with the posthumous title Minhui.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as grand preceptor, granted the privilege of an office equal to the three excellencies, enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, made pillar of state, and given the posthumous name Keen and Wise.

sentences.zh: 子六人，曰阿僧哥，大司徒；

translations.literal: He had six sons: the first, Asengge, Grand Preceptor;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons. The first, Asengge, became grand preceptor;

sentences.zh: 阿述臘，諸色人匠總管府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Ashula, Darughachi of the General Bureau of Supervisors of Artisan Households of All Categories.
translations.idiomatic: Ashula served as darughachi of the General Bureau of Supervisors of Artisan Households of All Categories.

sentences.zh: 有劉元者，嘗從阿尼哥學西天梵相，亦稱絕藝。

translations.literal: There was a Liu Yuan who had studied Western Heaven Buddhist images under Anige and was also called a consummate artist.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Liu Yuan who had studied Indian Buddhist images under Anige and was likewise acclaimed as a master of unsurpassed skill.

sentences.zh: 元字秉元，薊之寶坻人。

translations.literal: Yuan's courtesy name was Bingyuan; he was a native of Baodi in Ji prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan, courtesy name Bingyuan, was a native of Baodi in Ji prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始為黃冠，師事青州把道錄，傳其藝非一。

translations.literal: At first he was a Daoist priest and studied under the Daoist Registrar Ba of Qingzhou, from whom he received many arts.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Daoist priest and studied under Registrar Ba of Qingzhou, from whom he learned many crafts.

sentences.zh: 至元中，凡兩都名剎，塑土、范金、搏換為佛像，出元手者，神思妙合，天下稱之。

translations.literal: During the Zhiyuan period, among all the famous monasteries of the two capitals, Buddha images made of molded clay, cast metal, or boduo huan lacquer sculpture that came from Yuan's hand were marvels of inspired conception, and the realm acclaimed them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiyuan era, among the great monasteries of both capitals, clay, cast-metal, and boduo huan Buddha images from Liu Yuan's hand were marvels of inspired design, and the realm acclaimed them.

sentences.zh: 其上都三皇尤古粹，識者以為造意得三聖人之微者。

translations.literal: Especially his Three Sovereigns at Shangdu were ancient and refined in spirit; connoisseurs considered that in conception he had captured the subtle essence of the three sages.
translations.idiomatic: Above all, his Three Sovereigns at Shangdu were ancient and pure in spirit; connoisseurs said he had captured the subtle essence of the three sage-kings in his conception.

sentences.zh: 由是兩賜宮女為妻，命以官長其屬，行幸必從。

translations.literal: Therefore he was twice granted palace women as wives, appointed to an office to lead his subordinates, and whenever the emperor went on progress he always accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was twice granted palace women as wives, given an office to command his subordinates, and always accompanied the emperor on progress.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘗敕元非有旨不許為人造他神像。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong once issued an edict that Yuan was not permitted to make images of other deities for others unless there was an imperial command.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong once decreed that Liu Yuan might not make images of other deities for private patrons unless expressly ordered by the throne.

sentences.zh: 後大都南城作東嶽廟，元為造仁聖帝像，巍巍然有帝王之度，其侍臣像，乃若憂深思遠者。

translations.literal: Later, when the Eastern Peak Temple was built in the southern city of Dadu, Yuan made the image of the Emperor of Benevolence and Sagacity — towering and endowed with imperial majesty. His attendant ministers' images seemed men of deep worry and far-reaching thought.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Eastern Peak Temple was built in the southern city of Dadu, Liu Yuan made the image of the Emperor of Benevolence and Sagacity — towering, with true imperial bearing. The attendant ministers he sculpted seemed men of deep worry and far-reaching thought.

sentences.zh: 始元欲作侍臣像，久之未措手，適閱秘書圖畫，見唐魏徵像，矍然曰：「得之矣，非若此，莫稱為相臣者。」

translations.literal: At first Yuan wished to make the attendant ministers' images but for a long time had not begun. Happening to look through the Secretariat's collection of paintings, he saw a portrait of Wei Zheng of the Tang and started up, saying: "I have it! Without such a figure, none can be called a chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: At first Liu Yuan meant to sculpt the attendant ministers but for a long time could not begin. Browsing the Secretariat's collection of paintings, he came upon a portrait of Wei Zheng of Tang and started up, crying, "This is it! Without such a figure, none can be called a chancellor."

sentences.zh: 遽走廟中為之，即日成，士大夫觀者，咸嘆異焉。

translations.literal: He hurried to the temple and made it; that same day it was finished. Scholar-officials who came to view it all marveled.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to the temple and finished it that same day. Scholar-officials who came to see it all marveled.

sentences.zh: 其所為西番佛像多秘，人罕得見者。

translations.literal: Most of the Western Regions Buddha images he made were kept secret; few had chance to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the Western Regions Buddha images he made were kept secret, and few ever saw them.

sentences.zh: 元官為昭文館大學士、正奉大夫、秘書卿，以壽終。

translations.literal: Yuan's offices were Grand Academician of the Academy of Literary Brilliance, Grand Master for Proper Service, and Director of the Secretariat; he died at a ripe old age.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan held the offices of grand academician of the Academy of Literary Brilliance, grand master for proper service, and director of the Secretariat, and died at a ripe old age.

sentences.zh: 搏換者，漫帛土偶上而髹之，已而去其土，髹帛儼然成像云。

translations.literal: Boduo huan is a technique in which silk cloth is layered over a clay model and lacquered; afterward the clay is removed, and the lacquered silk stands forth as an image.
translations.idiomatic: Boduo huan is the hollow lacquer sculpture technique: silk cloth is layered over a clay model and lacquered; when the clay is removed, the lacquered silk shell remains as a finished image.
